correctness.rationale: The inversion identity sigma({a,b})=2n-a-b-1 follows by counting unselected higher indices; fixed marginals imply expected sigma=n-2 and reduce variance to E[(a+b-(n+1))^2]. For even n, only opposite pairs have zero cost and each vertex has a unique partner. For odd n, the central vertex has inclusion probability 2/n and all incident pair costs are >=1, giving a sharp LP-dual bound. Equality supports only outer mirror edges and a central triangle; marginal equations force all probabilities, proving uniqueness. Uniformity under all relabelings forces the uniform pair distribution and its sample-without-replacement variance (n+1)(n-2)/6. Exact-rational checker tested n=3..100 and independent SciPy/HiGHS LP found the stated optima n=3..18; analytical proof, not the computations, covers all n. The arbitrary tie convention is explicitly assumed.

value.rationale: The 2026 apportionment work explicitly motivates minimizing total envy variance when expectation cannot be changed. Two residual seats are the smallest genuinely pair-dependent randomization, and equal residues are extremal for unavoidable expected envy, so this is a natural structural subfamily rather than a tuned numerical slice. The unique all-n optimal law and exact parity obstruction give an explicit O(n)-description instead of only a generic LP, with a precise large anonymity-versus-risk cost: anonymous variance (n+1)(n-2)/6 versus optimal 0 or 2/n. This measures a real tension between equal-party symmetry and minimizing variability under the paper’s fixed index-tie convention; the convention dependence is disclosed.
